problem: 6. On the edges of a trihedral angle with vertex at point $S$, there are points $M, N$, and $K$ such that $S M^{2}+S N^{2}+S K^{2} \leq 12$. Find the area of triangle $S M N$, given that the angle $M S N$ is $30^{\circ}$, and the volume of the pyramid $S M N K$ is maximally possible.
solution:
Solution. Let's introduce the notations: $S M=m, S N=n, S K=k$.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_6cabcf1712d23d5ceb2bg-04.jpg?height=320&width=442&top_left_y=548&top_left_x=630)

The volume of the pyramid $S M N K$ is

$$
V=\frac{1}{3} S_{S M N} \cdot h=\frac{1}{6} m n \sin \alpha \cdot h=\frac{1}{6} m n \sin \alpha \cdot k \sin \beta=\frac{\sin \alpha \sin \beta}{6} m n k .
$$

The values of the angles $\alpha, \beta$ depend on the trihedral angle but not on the positions of the points $M, N, K$ on its edges. Therefore, the maximum volume of the pyramid $S M N K$ corresponds to the maximum value of the product $m \cdot n \cdot k$, given the condition $m^{2}+n^{2}+k^{2} \leq p$. From the inequality of the geometric mean and the arithmetic mean of three numbers, it follows that $\sqrt[3]{m^{2} n^{2} k^{2}} \leq \frac{m^{2}+n^{2}+k^{2}}{3} \leq \frac{p}{3}$

Equality is achieved when $m=n=k$. Then, when $m=n=k=\sqrt{\frac{p}{3}}$, the volume of the pyramid is maximized, and the area of the triangle $S M N$ takes the value $\frac{p \sin \alpha}{6}$. In our case, $p=12, \alpha=30^{\circ}$, so $S_{S M N}=1$.

Answer: $S_{S M N}=1$.

$$

If $x$ is the desired value, then the quadratic trinomial $f(t)=4 t^{2}+8([x]+1) t+4[x]^{2}-5[x]-19$ has a root $t=\{x\}$ on the interval $[0 ; 1)$.

Solving the inequality using the interval method, we get $[x] \in\left(-\frac{7}{4} ; t_{1}\right] \cup\left(1 ; t_{2}\right]$. problem: 2. Find the integers $n$ for which the expression $\frac{1}{12}\left(8 \sin \frac{\pi n}{10}-\sin \frac{3 \pi n}{10}+4 \cos \frac{\pi n}{5}+1\right)$ takes integer values.
solution:
Solution. Let's introduce the notation $t=\sin \frac{\pi n}{10} \in[-1 ; 1]$ and rewrite the original expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{12}\left(8 \sin \frac{\pi n}{10}-\sin \frac{3 \pi n}{10}+4 \cos \frac{\pi n}{5}+1\right)=\frac{1}{12}\left(8 t-\left(3 t-4 t^{3}\right)+4\left(1-2 t^{2}\right)+1\right)= \\
& =\frac{1}{12}\left(4 t^{3}-8 t^{2}+5 t+5\right)=f(t)
\end{aligned}
$$

We will investigate the function $f(t)$ on the interval $[-1 ; 1]$. Let's find the critical points of the function $f(t): f^{\prime}(t)=\frac{1}{12}\left(12 t^{2}-16 t+5\right)=0 \rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{l}t_{1}=1 / 2 \\ t_{2}=5 / 6\end{array}\right.$.

At the point $t=1 / 2$, the function $f(t)$ has a local maximum, $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$. At the point $t=\frac{5}{6}$, the function $f(t)$ has a local minimum, $f\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)=\frac{65}{216}$. Let's find the value of the function $f(t)$ at the endpoints of the interval: $f(-1)=-1, f(1)=\frac{1}{2}$. As a result, we get the range of the function $E_{f}=\left[-1 ; \frac{1}{2}\right]$. It includes two integer values $y=-1$ and $y=0$.

Case 1. $y=-1$. This value is achieved at one value of $t=-1$. Then $\sin \frac{\pi n}{10}=-1 \rightarrow \frac{\pi n}{10}=-\frac{\pi}{2}+2 \pi k \rightarrow n=20 k-5, k \in Z$

Case 2. $y=0$. Let's solve the equation $4 t^{3}-8 t^{2}+5 t+5=0 \rightarrow(2 t+1)\left(2 t^{2}-5 t+5\right)=0$. Thus, the cubic polynomial has a single root $t=-\frac{1}{2}$. Then $\sin \frac{\pi n}{10}=-\frac{1}{2} \rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{l}\frac{\pi n}{10}=-\frac{\pi}{6}+2 \pi k \rightarrow 3 n-60 k=-5(*) \\ \frac{\pi n}{10}=\frac{7 \pi}{6}+2 \pi k \rightarrow 3 n-60 k=7(* *)\end{array}\right.$

Equations (*) and (**) do not have solutions in integers, since their left sides are not divisible by 3.

Answer: $n=20 k-5, k \in Z$.

problem: 3. On a plane, there are 8 lines, 3 of which are parallel, and any two of the remaining five intersect. We consider all triangles with sides lying on these lines. What is the greatest and the least number of such triangles that can be found?
solution:
Solution. Let's introduce the notation: $P$ - the set of parallel lines, $p_{k}, k=1,2, \ldots, m$ - any line from $P$; $Q$ - the set of non-parallel lines, $q_{j}, j=1,2, \ldots, n$ - any line from $Q$. The maximum possible number of triangles is associated with such an arrangement of lines from $Q$ where no three of them pass through the same point (maximum number of vertices). Then the number of triangles that do not have vertices on lines from $P$ is $C_{m}^{3}$. The number of triangles, one side of which lies on a line from $P$ is $n \cdot C_{m}^{2}$. Two sides of a triangle lying on two lines from $P$ do not exist due to their parallelism. Thus,

$$
N_{\max }=C_{n}^{3}+m C_{n}^{2}=\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}+m \frac{n(n-1)}{2}=\frac{n(n-1)}{6}(n+3 m-2)
$$

The minimum possible number of triangles is associated with such an arrangement of lines from $Q$ where all lines $q_{j}$ pass through one point $A$. If $A$ does not belong to any of the lines $p_{k}, k=1,2, \ldots, m$, then the number of triangles is $N_{1}=m C_{n}^{2}$. If $A \in p_{k}$, then the number of the desired triangles is $N_{2}=(m-1) C_{n}^{2}$. Thus,

$$
N_{\min }=(m-1) C_{n}^{2}=\frac{(m-1) n(n-1)}{2}
$$

In our case $m=3, n=5$, and therefore $N_{\max }=40$, and $N_{\text {min }}=20$.

Answer: $N_{\max }=40, N_{\min }=20$.

1.2 Two weights with masses \( m_{1}=180 \) g and \( m_{2}=120 \) g hang from the ends of a weightless, inextensible string, which is passed over a fixed pulley. Initially, the weights were at the same level. The weights were released and came into motion without initial velocity. What will be the vertical distance between the weights after \(\Delta t=1.5\) s from the start of the motion? Air resistance and friction in the pulley can be neglected.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_6ec43fa2f035f1ec876bg-02.jpg?height=540&width=368&top_left_y=1746&top_left_x=136)

Let's write Newton's second law for the first and second weights \( m_{1,2}=T_{1,2}-m_{1,2} g \).

Considering the inextensibility and weightlessness of the string \(\left(a_{1}=-a_{2}\right)\) and \(T_{1}=T_{2}=T\), we obtain the expression for the magnitude of the acceleration of each weight

\[
a=\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}} g
\]

The magnitude of their relative acceleration is \(a_{\text{rel}}=2a\). Then the distance between the weights after time \(\Delta t\) will be

\[
\Delta h=\frac{a_{\text{rel}} \Delta t^{2}}{2}=\left(\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\right) g \Delta t^{2}
\]

Substituting the numerical values, we get \(\Delta h=\frac{180-120}{180+120} \cdot 10 \frac{M}{s^{2}} \cdot(1.5)^{2} s^{2}=4.5\) m.

1.4 An ideal monatomic gas is the working substance of a heat engine operating according to the thermodynamic cycle $1-2-3-1$. Find the efficiency of this heat engine if it is known that the maximum and minimum pressure values differ by a factor of $k=4$.

The efficiency by definition $\eta=\frac{A}{Q^{+}}$. The work can be easily determined as

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_6ec43fa2f035f1ec876bg-03.jpg?height=391&width=511&top_left_y=1775&top_left_x=156)
the area enclosed by the cycle $A=\frac{1}{2} P_{1}(k-1) V_{1}(k-1)$.

The heat received according to the first law of thermodynamics $Q^{+}=A_{23}+\Delta U_{13}$. The work on the segment $2-3$ is also found "graphically" $A_{23}=k P_{1} V_{1}(k-1)$.

The change in internal energy $\Delta U_{13}=\frac{3}{2} \Delta(P V)=$ $\frac{3}{2}\left(k^{2} P_{1} V_{1}-P_{1} V_{1}\right)$.

From the above relations, it follows:

$$
\eta=\frac{\frac{1}{2}(k-1)^{2}}{k(k-1)+\frac{3}{2}\left(k^{2}-1\right)}=\frac{k-1}{5 k+3}
$$

For $k=4$, the efficiency has the value $\eta=\frac{3}{23} \approx 13 \%$

problem: 1. (15 points) A small rubber ball moves between two massive vertical walls, colliding with them. One of the walls is stationary, while the other is moving away from it at a constant speed \( u = 100 \, \text{cm} / \text{s} \). Assuming the ball's motion is always horizontal and the collisions are perfectly elastic, find its final speed if the initial speed of the ball was \( v_{0} = 2017 \, \text{cm} / \text{s} \).
solution: 1. With each elastic collision with the moving wall, the direction of the ball's velocity changes to the opposite, and its speed relative to the Earth decreases by $2 u$, i.e., by 200 cm/s. Upon collision with the stationary wall, only the direction changes. Thus, after $n=10$ collisions with the moving wall and the same number with the stationary wall, the ball's speed will become $v=v_{0}-2 u n=17 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$, and the ball will no longer be able to catch up with the receding wall. (15 points)

problem: 2. (15 points) A satellite is launched vertically from the pole of the Earth at the first cosmic speed. To what maximum distance from the Earth's surface will the satellite travel? (The acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface $g=10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{c}^{2}$, radius of the Earth $R=6400$ km).
solution:
2. 

According to the law of conservation of energy: $\frac{m v_{I}^{2}}{2}-\frac{\gamma m M}{R}=-\frac{\gamma m M}{R+H}$

The first cosmic speed $v_{I}=\sqrt{g R}$

The acceleration due to gravity at the surface $g=\frac{\gamma M}{R^{2}}$

Then $\frac{m g R}{2}-m g R=-\frac{m g R^{2}}{R+H}$

Finally, $H=R=6400$ km.

(15 points)

problem: 3. (15 points) Determine the mass $m$ of helium needed to fill an empty balloon of mass $m_{1}=10$ g so that the balloon will rise. solution:
3. For the balloon to take off, the condition is $F_{\text {Arch }}=\left(m+m_{1}\right) g$

$F_{\text {Arch }}=\rho_{0} g V$

From the Clapeyron-Mendeleev equation, the density of air is

$\rho_{0}=\frac{P_{0} M_{\mathrm{B}}}{R T_{0}}, \quad$ and the volume of the balloon $V=\frac{m}{M_{\mathrm{r}}} \frac{R T_{0}}{P_{0}}$

Then $m \frac{M_{\mathrm{B}}}{M_{\mathrm{r}}}=\left(m+m_{1}\right)$

Finally, $m=\frac{m_{1} M_{\mathrm{r}}}{M_{\mathrm{B}}-M_{\mathrm{r}}}=1.6$ g.

problem: 4. (15 points) Carefully purified water can be supercooled to a temperature below $0^{\circ}$. However, if a crystal of ice is thrown into it, the water will immediately begin to freeze. What fraction of water supercooled to $-10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in a thermos will freeze if a small ice chip is thrown into it? solution:
4. A small ice crystal becomes a center of crystallization. The heat released during crystallization goes to heating the water. Eventually, thermal equilibrium is established at $t=0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

From the heat balance equation $\quad \lambda m_{\text{ice}}=c m_{\text{water}} \Delta t$

Finally $\quad \frac{m_{\text{ice}}}{m_{\text{water}}}=\frac{c \Delta t}{\lambda}=0.13$.

(15 points)

solution:

External minimal force at each moment in time

problem: 1. Dmitry is three times as old as Grigory was when Dmitry was as old as Grigory is now. When Grigory becomes as old as Dmitry is now, the sum of their ages will be 49 years. How old is Grigory?
solution: Solution: Let Gregory be $y$ years old in the past, and Dmitry be $x$ years old. Then currently, Gregory is $x$ years old, and Dmitry is $3 y$ years old. In the future, Gregory will be $3 y$ years old, and Dmitry will be $z$ years old, and according to the condition, $z+3 y=49$. Since $z-3 y=3 y-x ; 3 y-x=x-y$, then $9 y-x=49$ and $x=2 y$. From this, we get that $x=14, y=7$. Currently, Gregory is 14 years old. Answer: 14.

3. Find the rational number - the value of the expression

$$
2 \cos ^{6}(5 \pi / 16)+2 \sin ^{6}(11 \pi / 16)+3 \sqrt{2} / 8
$$
solution:
Solution: By the reduction formula, the desired expression is equal to

$2 \cos ^{6}(5 \pi / 16)+2 \sin ^{6}(5 \pi / 16)+3 \sqrt{2} / 8$. By the sum of cubes formula, we have:

$\cos ^{6}(5 \pi / 16)+\sin ^{6}(5 \pi / 16)=1-\frac{3 \sin ^{2}(10 \pi / 16)}{4}$. Therefore, our expression takes the form:

$2-\frac{3 \sin ^{2}(10 \pi / 16)}{2}+\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{8}=2-\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{1-\cos (5 \pi / 4)}{2}\right)+\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{8}=\frac{5}{4}$. Answer: 5/4.

problem: 4. Solve the equation $\frac{4}{\sqrt{\log _{3}(81 x)}+\sqrt{\log _{3} x}}+\sqrt{\log _{3} x}=3$.
solution: Solution: Using the properties of logarithms, our equation can be rewritten as $\frac{4}{\sqrt{4+\log _{3} x}+\sqrt{\log _{3} x}}+\sqrt{\log _{3} x}=3$. Let $t=\log _{3} x$. Then $\frac{4}{\sqrt{4+t}+\sqrt{t}}+\sqrt{t}=3$. Multiplying the numerator and denominator of the first fraction by $\sqrt{t+4}-\sqrt{t}$, we arrive at the equation $\sqrt{t+4}=3$. From this, we get that $t=5$ and $x=3^{5}=243$. Answer: 243.

problem: 5. Find the minimum value of the function $y=\sin 2x-(\sin x+\cos x)+1$.
solution:
Solution: Let $t=\sin x+\cos x$. Then $t^{2}=1+\sin 2 x$ and $y=t^{2}-t$.

In this case, $t \in[-\sqrt{2} ; \sqrt{2}]$. This function reaches its minimum at $t=1 / 2$ and this minimum is equal to $-1 / 4$. Answer: $-1 / 4$.

problem: 6. The sum of $n$ terms of the geometric progression $\left\{b_{n}\right\}$ is 6 times less than the sum of their reciprocals. Find the product $b_{1} b_{n}$.
solution:
Solution: Let $S_{n}=b_{1}+b_{2}+\ldots+b_{n}, S_{n}^{1}=\frac{1}{b_{1}}+\frac{1}{b_{2}}+\ldots+\frac{1}{b_{n}} \cdot$ Then

$b_{1} b_{n} S_{n}^{1}=\frac{b_{1} b_{n}}{b_{1}}+\frac{b_{1} b_{n}}{b_{2}}+\ldots+\frac{b_{1} b_{n}}{b_{n}}=b_{n}+b_{n-1}+\ldots+b_{1}=S_{n}$. From this we obtain: $b_{1} b_{n}=\frac{S_{n}}{S_{n}^{1}}=\frac{1}{6}$.

Answer: $1 / 6$

problem: 7. Solve the system of equations $\left\{\begin{array}{c}x^{4}-y^{4}=3 \sqrt{|y|}-3 \sqrt{|x|} \\ x^{2}-2 x y=27\end{array}\right.$.
solution: Solution: Write the system as $\left\{\begin{array}{c}x^{4}+3 \sqrt{|x|}=y^{4}+3 \sqrt{|y|} \\ x^{2}-2 x y=27\end{array}\right.$. The function $z=s^{4}+3 \sqrt{|s|}$ is even and, moreover, it is increasing on $[0 ;+\infty)$. Therefore, from the first equation, we find that $x=y$ or $x=-y$. Substituting $x=y$ into the second equation, we see that there are no solutions. If $x=-y$, then $x_{1}=3, y_{1}=-3 ; x_{2}=-3 ; y_{2}=3$. Answer: $\pm(3,-3)$.

solution:

problem: 10. For what values of the parameter $a$ does the equation $x^{4}-20 x^{2}+64=a\left(x^{2}+6 x+8\right)$ have exactly three distinct solutions?
solution:
Solution: Factorize the right and left sides of the equation:

\((x-2)(x+2)(x-4)(x+4)=a(x+2)(x+4)\). The equation can be written as \((x+2)(x+4)\left(x^{2}-6 x+8-a\right)=0\). It is obvious that -2 and -4 are roots of this equation. We are satisfied with the situation where exactly one of the roots of the equation \(x^{2}-6 x+8-a=0\) does not coincide with -2 and -4. The total number of solutions will be three if the last equation has one root \(x_{3}\), and \(x_{3} \neq x_{1}, x_{3} \neq x_{2}\), or if this equation has two roots \(x_{3}, x_{4}\), one of which coincides with \(x_{1}\) or \(x_{2}\). The equation \(x^{2}-6 x+8-a=0\) has one root when \(a=-1\) and this root is different from the specified numbers. The numbers -2 and -4 are roots of the last equation when \(a=24\) and \(a=48\), and in these cases, the second roots are different from -2 and -4. Answer: \(a=-1 ; 24 ; 48\).

problem: 9. At the base of the quadrilateral pyramid $S A B C D$ lies the quadrilateral $A B C D$, in which $A B=A D=6, C B=C D=2$, and sides $A B$ and $B C$ are mutually perpendicular. All lateral faces are inclined to the base plane at an angle of $60^{\circ}$. Find the volume $V$ of the pyramid, knowing that $V>12$.
solution:
Solution: At the base of the pyramid lies a quadrilateral composed of two equal right-angled triangles. The area of the base is $S=6 \cdot 2=12$. Since the lateral faces are inclined to the base plane at the same angle, the apex of the pyramid projects onto the base plane at a point equidistant from the lines $A B, B C, C D, D A$. The apex can project onto the center of the circle inscribed in the quadrilateral $A B C D$, or onto the center of the exscribed circle. In the first case, let $r$ be the radius of the inscribed circle and note that the area of the base $S=p r$, where $p-$ is the semiperimeter of the base, $p=A B+B C=8$. The radius of the inscribed circle $r=\frac{S}{p}=\frac{12}{8}=\frac{3}{2}$. The height of the pyramid $H=r \operatorname{tg} 60^{\circ}=3 \sqrt{3} / 2$. The volume of the pyramid $V=\frac{1}{3} S H=6 \sqrt{3}12$

ANSWER: $12 \sqrt{3}$.

In each of the following paragraphs, select all incorrect statements and/or actions and explain why they are incorrect.

For convenience, the paragraphs of the task text are numbered. In your answer, indicate the number of the corresponding paragraph and your comment on it.

[1] Olga bought a car and decided to insure it. She knows that the most important thing is to get a compulsory third-party liability insurance (OSAGO) policy, without which it is impossible to drive a car. This policy will protect both her life and health and her car from material damage from third parties. Even if an accident occurs due to Olga's fault, the insurance company that issued the OSAGO policy will fully cover the repair of her own car within the insurance amount and the cars of the victims, regardless of their cost.

[2] Olga is confident that when calculating the OSAGO policy, the insurance company will take into account such factors as the make of the car, the color of its body, Olga's nationality, her racial affiliation, family status, education, religion, and position. In addition, Olga believes that as a mother of several children, she is entitled to a federal benefit when purchasing this policy.

[3] Olga also thinks about buying a comprehensive insurance (KASKO) policy to protect herself from the risks of damage and theft. At the time of concluding the insurance contract, the actual value of the car is 750,000 rubles, but Olga thinks it would be better to insure it for a larger amount, for example, 1,000,000 rubles. She is willing to pay more for the KASKO policy because this will allow her to count on a larger insurance payout. In addition, Olga is considering increasing her insurance protection by buying a second KASKO policy from another insurance company and insuring her car against the same risks and for the same insurance amount.

[4] To save on the cost of OSAGO and KASKO policies, Olga is considering including an unconditional deductible in the insurance contracts, as she believes that she can cover minor damage at her own expense. If the amount of damage to the car exceeds the deductible, the insurance company will fully compensate for the losses.

[5] If Olga plans to drive her car to another Russian region, she will get a "Green Card," which will protect her car both from material damage from third parties and from theft.

[6] When choosing an insurance company, Olga should check whether it has a license issued by the Federal Insurance Supervision Service and the validity period of the license. The longer the validity period of the issued license, the more reliable the insurance company.

## Solution and Evaluation Criteria

[1] OSAGO does not insure the life and health of the policyholder or the car of the policyholder from material damage from third parties. OSAGO is compulsory insurance of the civil liability of the policyholder (1 point) for causing harm to life (1 point) and health (1 point), as well as property of third parties (1 point).

If Olga is at fault in an accident, she will not receive anything under the OSAGO policy. (1 point) The insurance company will compensate the victims for the damage caused by Olga (1 point) within the insurance limits set by law (1 point).

[2] Insurance companies are not allowed to base the size of the base tariff on nationality (1 point), racial affiliation (1 point), religion (1 point), political views (1 point), and position of the car owner (1 point). Insurance companies can take into account any other factors when calculating the cost of the OSAGO policy, provided they are supported by statistical data on the number of accidents and the amounts of insurance payouts for different individual characteristics of drivers and their vehicles.

No benefits are provided when purchasing an OSAGO policy. (1 point)

[3] The insurance amount cannot exceed the actual value at the time of concluding the contract. (1 point)

If Olga insures her car against the same risks in another insurance company and the total insurance amount exceeds the value of the insured property, this will be considered double insurance. (2 points)

[4] Olga is confusing an absolute deductible and a conditional deductible. The amount of an absolute deductible is always deducted from the insurance payout (i.e., the insurance payout is calculated as the difference between the amount of the loss and the amount of the deductible), unlike a conditional deductible, where the insurer is exempt from compensating the loss if its amount does not exceed the amount of the deductible and fully compensates the loss if the amount of the loss exceeds the amount of the deductible. (2 points)

A deductible can be included in a KASKO policy, but not in an OSAGO policy. (1 point)

[5] There is no need to obtain a special compulsory insurance policy for driving a car in another region. (1 point)

The "Green Card" is essentially an equivalent of OSAGO (1 point), i.e., it insures the civil liability of the policyholder to third parties (1 point), but it is only valid when the car is abroad. (1 point)

[6] Insurance licenses are issued by the Bank of Russia. (1 point)

Licenses are issued without a validity period, so it is meaningless to focus on the validity period of the issued license. (1 point)

## Task 4 (20 points)

Olga Petrovna is considering the possibility of participating in a certain business project. She needs to immediately invest 2 million rubles of her own money (which is currently in a bank deposit). Additionally, she will need to invest another 1 million rubles exactly one year later, which Olga Petrovna will have to borrow. However, according to her calculations, the project will generate 3 million 795 thousand rubles of net income exactly two years from now.

For simplicity, assume that the interest rates on deposits and loans are the same and equal to $r\%$ per year; interest is accrued and capitalized at the end of the year; there is no inflation; and investment risks are negligible.

Within what range should the interest rate $r$ be for Olga Petrovna not to lose interest in this business project?
solution:
# Solution and Evaluation Criteria:

Let's bring all cash flows to the present moment.

Revenues of 3.795 million rubles in two years are equivalent to 3.795/(1+r)^2 in present value (5 points)

Expenses of 1 million rubles in one year are equivalent to 1/(1+r) in present value (5 points)

The business project will be interesting if the revenues exceed the expenses, i.e., 3.795/(1+r)^2 > 2 + 1/(1+r) (2 points)

From this, we find that r < 0.15 (i.e., 15%) (5 points)

Answer: r < 15%

Notes. A common mistake is attempting to account for the 2 million rubles twice, both in the calculation of the alternative return and as an investment in the business project (when 2 is subtracted from 3.795 in the last expression).

Minus 2.5 points for those who took the ready-made rate of 15% and proved that at this rate NPV = 0. A penalty (up to 2.5 points) may be applied for the lack of comments in cases where the logic of the solution is not clear without them.

problem:
1. Over three years, Marina did not invest funds from her Individual Investment Account (IIS) into financial instruments and therefore did not receive any income from the IIS. However, she still acquired the right to an investment tax deduction for contributing personal funds to the IIS (Article 291.1 of the Tax Code of the Russian Federation).

The tax deduction is provided in the amount of funds deposited in the tax period into the IIS, but not exceeding 400,000 rubles in total per year.

Marina is entitled to receive 13% of the amount deposited into the IIS from the state in the form of a refunded personal income tax (NDFL) that she paid to the treasury from her income.

The amount of NDFL deducted from Marina's annual salary = 30000 * 12 months * 0.13 = 46800 rubles.

The tax deduction for the first year = 100000 * 0.13 = 13000 rubles. This amount does not exceed the amount of NDFL deducted from Marina's annual salary.

The tax deduction for the second year = 400000 * 0.13 = 52000 rubles. This amount exceeds the amount of NDFL deducted from Marina's annual salary. Therefore, the tax deduction will be limited to the amount of NDFL paid for the second year of the IIS's existence, or 46800 rubles.

The tax deduction for the third year = 400000 * 0.13 = 52000 rubles. This amount also exceeds the amount of NDFL deducted from Marina's annual salary. Therefore, the tax deduction will be limited to the amount of NDFL paid for the third year, or 46800 rubles.

The total tax deduction over 3 years = 13000 + 46800 + 46800 = 106600 rubles.

The return on Marina's operations over 3 years = 106600 / 1000000 * 100% = 10.66%.

The annual return on Marina's operations = 10.66% / 3 = 3.55%.

Alexander Ivanovich has 300,000 rubles, for which he is considering three possible investment options: investing in his neighbor's business, buying a security, and purchasing a plot of land on the Moon. Each investment option will either bring a 20% profit (50 chances out of 100) or a 20% loss (50 chances out of 100). Assume that the chances of earning profits/losses for the three options are completely unrelated to each other (i.e., the fact that the first option brings a profit does not change the chances that the second and third options will bring a profit/loss).

Calculate the probability that Alexander Ivanovich will incur a significant loss from his investment activities (Alexander Ivanovich considers a significant loss to be a 20% or greater loss from the initially invested 300,000 rubles) if...

a) He invests all 300,000 rubles in currency (2 points);

b) He invests 150,000 rubles in a security and 150,000 rubles in his neighbor's business (4 points);

c) He invests 100,000 rubles in a security, 100,000 rubles in his neighbor's business, and 100,000 rubles in lunar land plots (9 points).

Answers:

a) One chance in two (or 50 out of 100)

b) One chance in four (or 25 out of 100)

c) One chance in eight (or 12.5 out of 100)
solution:
Solution.

a) The chances of incurring a loss when investing in a security are 50 out of 100 (or, in other words, one chance in 2), which directly follows from the condition.

b) Let's consider all possible combinations of options:

| Combination | Security | Neighbor's Business | Investment Result |

| 2 | Profit: 180000 | Profit: 180000 | 360000 |
| 3 | Loss: 120000 | Loss: 120000 | 240000 |
| 4 | Loss: 120000 | Profit: 180000 | 300000 |

If the probabilities of profits/losses are not related to each other, then each combination has an equal chance of realization. This means that

- 25 chances out of 100 that Mr. Ivanovich will receive 360,000, i.e., earn.
- 50 chances out of 100 that Mr. Ivanovich will "break even."
- 25 chances out of 100 that Mr. Ivanovich will receive 240,000, losing $20\%$ of the investment.

The chances of incurring a 20% loss are 25 out of 100 (or one chance in 4).

c) Let's consider all possible combinations of options:

| Combination | Security | Neighbor's Business | Lunar Plot | Investment Result |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | Profit: 120000 | Profit: 120000 | Profit: 120000 | 360000 |
| $\overline{2}$ | Profit: 120000 | Profit: 120000 | Loss: 80000 | 320000 |
| 3 | Profit: 120000 | Loss: 80000 | Profit: 120000 | 320000 |

| 8 | Loss: 80000 | Loss: 80000 | Loss: 80000 | 240000 |

By conducting an analysis similar to point b), it can be shown that in this case, the chances of incurring a 20% loss are 12.5 out of 100 (or one chance in 8). There are also three chances out of 8 that Mr. Ivanovich will lose part of his investment, but only $10\%$. Diversification of investments reduces the probability of significant losses!

\end{array} \rightarrow \left\{\begin{array}{c}
\cos x=1 / 2+k, k \in Z \\

m=3 \\
m=-3
\end{array}\right.
$$

problem: 2. To fight against the mice, the cat Leopold must drink animalin daily. The cat has a bottle of animalin solution in water (a colorless transparent liquid) with a volume of $V=0.5$ l and a volumetric concentration of animalin $C_{0}=40 \%$. Every day, Leopold drinks $v=50$ ml of the solution, and to avoid being noticed by the mice, he adds the same volume of water to the bottle. Find the volumetric concentration of animalin in the bottle after the cat has drunk $n=5$ times, each time $v=50$ ml of liquid, and after each time, added water to the bottle.
solution:
2. Let's find the change in the concentration of the absinthe solution after the cat drinks one portion. By definition of volume concentration,

$$
C_{0}=\frac{v_{O}}{V}
$$

where $C_{0}$ is the volume concentration of the solution, $v_{o}$ is the initial volume of absinthe in the bottle, and $V$ is the total volume of the solution. Therefore, after the cat drinks $v$ ml of the solution, the remaining volume of absinthe is

$$
v_{O}^{\prime}=C_{0}(V-v)
$$

Since the volume of the solution returns to $V$ after adding water, the new volume concentration of the solution $C_{1}$ is

$$
C_{1}=\frac{v_{o}^{\prime}}{V}=\frac{C_{0}(V-v)}{V}=C_{0}\left(1-\frac{v}{V}\right)
$$

After the cat drinks the second portion of absinthe, the concentration in the solution is found similarly:

$$
C_{2}=C_{1}\left(1-\frac{v}{V}\right)=C_{0}\left(1-\frac{v}{V}\right)^{2}
$$

Therefore, after the cat drinks $n$ portions of absinthe (refilling the bottle with water after each drink), the concentration of absinthe in the bottle will be

$$
C_{5}=C_{0}\left(1-\frac{v}{V}\right)^{n}=23.6 \%
$$

problem:
3. A cyclic process $1-2-3-4-1$ is carried out with an ideal gas, consisting of two isotherms (2-3 and 4-1) and two isochors ($1-2$ and $3-4$; see figure). It is known that the ratio of temperatures on the isotherms 2-3 and 4-1 is $T_{2-3} / T_{4-1}=3$, and that during the isothermal expansion, the gas received twice as much heat as during the isochoric heating. Find the efficiency of the cycle.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_2fcbf33eea2a4c6aa801g-1.jpg?height=309&width=448&top_left_y=979&top_left_x=1478)
solution:
3. Let the gas receive an amount of heat $Q$ during the isothermal expansion segment. Then, according to the condition, the gas receives an amount of heat $Q / 2$ during the isochoric heating segment. Therefore, the total amount of heat received by the gas from the heater during the cycle is

$$
Q_{n}=\frac{3}{2} Q
$$

Now, let's find the work done by the gas. Work is done only in the processes 2-3 and 4-1, and the magnitude of the work done by the gas in these processes differs by a factor of three (since at the same volume, the pressure in process 2-3 is three times greater than the pressure in process 4-1, and work is the area under the process curve in the $p-V$ coordinates). Therefore, the work done by the gas during the cycle is

$$
A=Q-\frac{1}{3} Q=\frac{2}{3} Q
$$

From this, we can find the efficiency of the cycle

$$
\eta=\frac{A}{Q_{u}}=\frac{4}{9}
$$

problem:
4. The electrical circuit shown in the figure contains a very large number of identical resistors and identical voltmeters. It is known that the readings of voltmeters $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ are $U=4$ V and $U^{\prime}=6$ V (although it is unknown which reading corresponds to which voltmeter). Find the readings of voltmeters $V_{3}$ and $V_{4}$, as well as the sum of the readings of all voltmeters.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_2fcbf33eea2a4c6aa801g-1.jpg?height=266&width=691&top_left_y=1295&top_left_x=1248)
solution:
4. Since the current flowing through the voltmeter $V_{1}$ is greater than the current flowing through the voltmeter $V_{2}$, the resistances of the voltmeters are the same, and each voltmeter shows the voltage across it, the value $U^{\prime}=6$ V is the reading of the voltmeter $V_{1}$, $U=4$ V is the reading of the voltmeter $V_{2}$, and the ratio of the currents flowing through the voltmeters $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ is

$$
\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\frac{U^{\prime}}{U}=\frac{3}{2} \quad \Rightarrow \quad I_{2}=\frac{2}{3} I_{1}
$$

Since the current flowing through the voltmeter $V_{1}$ is divided into the currents flowing through $V_{2}$ and $V_{3}$, the current flowing through the voltmeter $V_{3}$ is

$$
I_{3}=\frac{1}{3} I_{1}
$$

Therefore, the resistance of the circuit segment shown in the figure on the right is twice the resistance of the voltmeter $R_{x}=2 R$, where $R$ is the resistance of the voltmeter, and $R_{x}$ is the resistance of the circuit segment shown in the figure. On the other hand, if one link is removed from the infinite circuit, its resistance does not change.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_69aec43348e730276044g-2.jpg?height=257&width=488&top_left_y=1479&top_left_x=1475)

Therefore, the resistance of the circuit shown in the figure is also equal to $R_{x}$. Hence,

$$
R_{x}=r+R+\frac{R R_{x}}{R+R_{x}}
$$

where $r$ is the resistance of the resistor. Considering that $R_{x}=2 R$, we find

$$
r=\frac{R}{3}
$$

Therefore, the voltage across the resistor in the first link of the considered circuit $U_{r}=2 \mathrm{~V}$, and the voltage created by the source across the entire circuit is

$$
U=U_{r}+U^{\prime}+U=12 \mathrm{~V} .
$$

The voltage applied to the second link of our circuit is three times less, $U=4$ V. This means that the readings of the voltmeters in the second link of the circuit $V_{3}$ and $V_{4}$ will be three times less than the readings of the voltmeters in the first link

$$
U_{3}=2 \mathrm{~V}, U_{4}=\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{~V}
$$

That is, their sum will be equal to

$$
U_{3}+U_{4}=\frac{10}{3}=\frac{1}{3}\left(U_{1}+U_{2}\right)
$$

Similarly, the sum of the readings of the voltmeters $V_{5}$ and $V_{6}$ will be one third of the sum of the readings of the voltmeters $V_{3}$ and $V_{4}$

$$
U_{5}+U_{6}=\frac{1}{3}\left(U_{3}+U_{4}\right)=\frac{1}{9}\left(U_{1}+U_{2}\right)
$$

From this, we conclude that the sum of the readings of all voltmeters will be equal to

$$
\sum U=U_{1}+U_{2}+U_{3}+U_{4}+\ldots=\left(U_{1}+U_{2}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{9}+\ldots\right)
$$

Finding the sum of the geometric progression in parentheses, we get

$$
\sum U=\frac{3}{2}\left(U+U^{\prime}\right)=15 \mathrm{~V}
$$

$$

We will calculate $\cos 2 \alpha$:

$$
\sin ^{2} \alpha=1-\cos ^{2} \alpha=1-\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{4}=\frac{2-\sqrt{3}}{4} \rightarrow \cos 2 \alpha=\cos ^{2} \alpha-\sin ^{2} \alpha=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \rightarrow 2 \alpha=30^{\circ}

problem:
3. (physics) A wire is made into a right-angled triangle with legs of length $l=1$ m. From vertices A and B, two bugs start crawling along the legs simultaneously with speeds $v_{A}=5$ cm/s and $v_{B}=2 v_{A}=10$ cm/s (see figure). What is the minimum time after the start of their movement when the distance between the bugs reaches a minimum?

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_25c5d6100f66704b4a85g-2.jpg?height=354&width=354&top_left_y=1770&top_left_x=1545)
solution:
Solution. Let the time that has passed since the beetles started moving be $t$. Then beetle

A will travel a distance of $v_{A} t$, beetle B - a distance of $v_{B} t=2 v_{A} t$. Therefore, the distance $S$ between the beetles at this moment will be

$$
S=\sqrt{\left(l-v_{A} t\right)^{2}+4 v_{A}^{2} t^{2}}
$$

We will find the minimum value of $S$ as a function of time. For this, we will differentiate the function $S(t)$, set the derivative to zero, and solve the resulting equation. Moreover, it is technically more convenient to differentiate $S^{2}$ rather than $S$, as the expressions will be much simpler, and both $S$ and $S^{2}$ reach their maximum at the same value of the argument. Thus,

$$
\left(S^{2}\right)^{\prime}=-2\left(l-v_{A} t\right) v_{A}+8 v_{A}^{2} t
$$

Setting the derivative (**) to zero, we get an equation for the time that has passed from the start of the movement until the moment when the distance between the beetles is the smallest

$$
l-v_{A} t=4 v_{A} t
$$

From which

$$
t=\frac{l}{5 v_{A}}=4 \mathrm{~s}
$$

problem: 4. (Physics) Find the total resistance of the electrical circuit, the scheme of which is shown in the figure. The values of all resistances are given in the figure. $r=1$ Ohm.
solution:

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_25c5d6100f66704b4a85g-3.jpg?height=251&width=442&top_left_y=734&top_left_x=1458)
$I$, which splits at the first branching into currents $I_{1}$ (in the lower leg of the circuit) and $I-I_{1}$ (in the upper leg; see the figure). Due to the symmetry of the section, after the middle resistance $r$, the currents will swap places - $I-I_{1}$ in the lower leg, and $I_{1}$ in the upper. Therefore, through the middle resistance $r$, the electric current $2 I_{1}-I$ (from the lower node to the upper) flows, and the potential difference between these nodes can be found using Ohm's law for the circuit section

$$
\varphi_{2}-\varphi_{1}=r\left(2 I_{1}-I\right)
$$

On the other hand, the potential difference between these nodes can be found using Ohm's law for the upper section with resistance $r$ and the lower section with resistance $2 r$

$$
\varphi_{2}-\varphi_{1}=\left(\varphi_{0}-\varphi_{1}\right)-\left(\varphi_{0}-\varphi_{2}\right)=r\left(I-I_{1}\right)-2 r I_{1}=r\left(I-3 I_{1}\right)
$$

Equating formulas (*) and ( ${ }^{* *}$ ), we get

$$
2 I_{1}-I=I-3 I_{1}
$$

From this, we find the current $I_{1}=\frac{2}{5} I$ and the potential difference between the left and right nodes of the circuit

$$
\varphi_{0}-\varphi_{3}=\frac{3}{5} I r+\frac{2}{5} I 2 r=\frac{7}{5} I r .
$$

Therefore,

$$
R_{o \sigma}=\frac{7}{5} r=1.4 \text { Ohms. }
$$

problem: 5. The star "tau" in the constellation Cetus has a planetary system. On the third planet from the star, there is a very unusual gravity: the acceleration due to gravity is $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{c}^{2}$ up to a height of $h=10$ m from the surface, but above that, it is half as much. An astronaut throws a body straight up from the surface of the planet with a speed such that on Earth it would rise to a height of $H=20$ m. To what height above the surface of this planet will the body rise?
solution:
5. Since the height of the body's rise on Earth is $H$, the initial velocity of the thrown body is

$$
v_{0}=\sqrt{2 g H}
$$

On the planet from the "tau Ceti" system, the body will move to a height $h$ with acceleration $g$, and then with acceleration $g / 2$. Therefore, above this boundary, the body will rise to a height

$$
h_{0}=\frac{v_{1}^{2}}{2(g / 2)}=\frac{v_{1}^{2}}{g}
$$

where $v_{1}$ is the speed the body had at height $h$ from the surface. Let's find this speed. While the body was moving with acceleration $g$, the laws of its motion had the form

$$
\begin{aligned}
& x(t)=v_{0} t-\frac{g t^{2}}{2} \\
& v_{x}(t)=v_{0}-g t
\end{aligned}
$$

The body will rise to height $h$ in such a time $t_{1}$, which is determined from the equation

$$
\frac{g t_{1}^{2}}{2}-v_{0} t_{1}+h=0
$$

Solving this quadratic equation, we get

$$
\left(t_{1}\right)_{1,2}=\frac{v_{0} \pm \sqrt{v_{0}^{2}-2 g h}}{g}
$$

(we need the smaller root - with the minus sign). Substituting this time into the second equation (*), we find the speed of the body at the moment of acceleration change

$$
v_{1}=v_{x}\left(t_{1}\right)=\sqrt{v_{0}^{2}-2 g h}
$$

Substituting this speed into expression (*), we find the height of the body's rise above the level where its acceleration changes

$$
h_{0}=\frac{v_{0}^{2}-2 g h}{g}=\frac{v_{0}^{2}}{g}-2 h
$$

Therefore, above the planet's surface, the body will rise to a height

$$
H_{1}=h+h_{0}=\frac{v_{0}^{2}}{g}-h
$$

Substituting now this value of the initial velocity into this formula, we get finally

$$
H_{1}=2 H-h=30 \mathrm{~m}
$$

problem:
6. A sphere of radius $R$, made of a material with a density equal to that of water, floats in water, touching its surface (see figure). Find the force with which the water acts on the lower half of the sphere. The density of water $\rho$ is known.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_68830dad9e31db52b84ag-1.jpg?height=243&width=326&top_left_y=1986&top_left_x=1593)
solution:
6. Obviously, the forces acting on different parts of the surface of the lower hemisphere from the water are different and are also directed differently. Therefore, calculating this force by summing the forces acting on small elements of the hemisphere's surface is quite complex. However, we have another method of summation. The fact is that similar sums of forces over the surface of a body are included in Archimedes' law. Therefore, if we take an auxiliary body such that the lower surface of the sphere is its surface, and use Archimedes' law, we can calculate the required force.

Thus, let's mentally cut and remove the upper hemisphere, i.e., consider a body in the form of only the lower hemisphere. On one hand, the Archimedes force acting on this hemisphere from the water is known to us. This is

$$
F_{A}=\rho g V_{\text {n.u. }}=\frac{2}{3} \pi \rho g R^{3}
$$

where $\rho$ is the density of the water, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity, and $V_{n . u .}=2 \pi R^{3} / 3$ is the volume of the hemisphere. On the other hand, this force is the resultant of the forces acting on the hemisphere from the liquid. Therefore, it can be represented

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_da4bcdfbf884c3803425g-5.jpg?height=252&width=314&top_left_y=151&top_left_x=1613)
as the sum of the forces, one of which acts on the lower surface of the hemisphere $\vec{F}_{n . u .}$ (which we need to find), and the second acts on its flat circular surface closing the hemisphere $\vec{F}_{\kappa p}$. Since these forces are directed oppositely, in the expression for the Archimedes force, they are subtracted

$$
F_{A}=F_{n . u .}-F_{\kappa p}
$$

The last force is easy to calculate. Since the circular surface closing the hemisphere is at a depth $R$ in the liquid, the hydrostatic pressure of the liquid at this depth is $p=\rho g R$. Therefore,

$$
F_{\kappa p}=p \pi R^{2}=\pi \rho g R^{3}
$$

From here and formulas $(*),(* *)$ we find

$$
F_{n . u .}=F_{A}+F_{\kappa p}=\frac{5}{3} \pi \rho g R^{3}
$$

$$

Keeping the same notation, we assume that $x, y$, and $z$ are integers that can take negative values, with $|x| \leq 4,|y| \leq 3,|z| \leq 2$. In this case, the equilibrium condition takes the form of the equation

$$
2 x+3 y+5 z=12
$$

Let $z=t \in[-2 ; 2]$. Then, solving the Diophantine equation,
$2 x+3 y=12-5 t \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{c}x=5 t-12-3 s \\ y=12-5 t+2 s, s \in Z\end{array}\right.$

Case 1. $t=-2$

$\left\{\begin{array}{c}x=-22-3 s \\ y=22+2 s, s \in Z\end{array} \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{c}|22+3 s| \leq 4 \rightarrow s=-8,-7,-6 \\ |22+2 s| \leq 3 \rightarrow s=-13,-12,-11,-10\end{array} \rightarrow s \in \varnothing\right.\right.$

$\left\{\begin{array}{c}x=-7-3 s \\ y=7+2 s, s \in Z\end{array} \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{c}|7+3 s| \leq 4 \rightarrow s=-1,-2,-3 \\ |7+2 s| \leq 3 \rightarrow s=-2,-3,-4,-5\end{array} \rightarrow s_{3}=-2 \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=-1 \\ y=3, s_{4}=-3 \\ z=1\end{array} \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=2 \\ y=1 \\ z=1\end{array}\right.\right.\right.\right.$

$\left\{\begin{array}{c}x=-2-3 s \\ y=2+2 s, s \in Z\end{array} \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{l}|2+3 s| \leq 4 \rightarrow s=0,-1,-2 \\ |2+2 s| \leq 3 \rightarrow s=0,-1,-2\end{array} \rightarrow s_{5}=0 \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=-2 \\ y=2,2 \\ z=2\end{array},-1 \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=1 \\ y=0 \\ z=2\end{array}\right.\right.\right.\right.$

problem: 3. (physics) In a vessel, there is a mixture of equal masses of nitrogen $N_{2}$ and helium He at a pressure $p$. The absolute temperature of the gas is doubled, during which all nitrogen molecules dissociate into atoms. Find the pressure of the gas mixture at this temperature. The molar masses of the gases are $\mu_{\text {He }}=4$ g/mol, $\mu_{N_{2}}=28$ g/mol. The gases are considered ideal.
solution:
Solution. Let the mass of helium and nitrogen in the vessel be $m$. Then Dalton's law for the initial gas mixture gives

$$
p=\frac{v_{\mathrm{He}} R T}{V}+\frac{v_{N_{2}} R T}{V}
$$

where

$$
v_{N_{2}}=\frac{m}{\mu_{N_{2}}}=v ; \quad v_{\mathrm{He}}=\frac{m}{\mu_{\mathrm{He}}}=7 v
$$

are the amounts of substance of nitrogen and helium in the vessel, $V$ - its volume. From this, we have for the initial pressure of the mixture

$$
p=\frac{8 v R T}{V}
$$

After heating, the vessel will contain a mixture of atomic nitrogen and helium. The amount of substance of atomic nitrogen after dissociation doubles, the amount of substance of helium remains unchanged

$$
v_{N}^{\prime}=2 v ; \quad v_{H e}^{\prime}=7 v
$$

Therefore, the pressure in the vessel will be equal to

$$
p^{\prime}=\frac{v_{H e}^{\prime} R 2 T}{V}+\frac{v_{N}^{\prime} R 2 T}{V}=\frac{7 v R 2 T}{V}+\frac{2 v R 2 T}{V}=\frac{18 v R T}{V}=\frac{9}{4} p
$$

4. (physics) Two bodies with masses $m$ and $2 m$ are connected by ropes. One rope is thrown over a pulley, the axis of which is attached to the ceiling. Another rope has the same pulley placed on it, to the axis of which a body with mass $4 m$ is attached (see figure). Find the tension force in the rope connecting the bodies $m$ and $2 m$ through the upper pulley. The ropes are inextensible and weightless. The pulleys are weightless and can

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_7d3a82aa7ed091c0d22dg-4.jpg?height=332&width=206&top_left_y=448&top_left_x=1690)
rotate without friction.
solution:
Solution. Since the blocks do not move (only rotate), the acceleration of the body with mass $4 m$ is zero. Therefore, the tension force in the lower rope connecting the bodies $m$ and $2 m$ is

$$
T_{u}=2 \mathrm{mg}
$$

Newton's second law for the bodies with masses $m$ and $2 m$ in projections on the axis directed vertically downward has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}
& 2 m g+T_{n}-T_{\sigma}=2 m a \\
& m g+T_{n}-T_{\sigma}=-m a
\end{aligned}
$$

where $T_{\varepsilon}$ is the tension force in the rope connecting the bodies $m$ and $2 m$ and passing over the upper block. In (*) it is taken into account that the accelerations of the bodies $m$ and $2 m$ are equal in magnitude and oppositely directed. Subtracting these equations, we find $a=g / 3$. From this,

$$
T_{\varepsilon}=\frac{10}{3} m g
$$

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_95ebfad0f8dcea9468d4g-1.jpg?height=319&width=505&top_left_y=2122&top_left_x=1415)
process. How much work does the gas perform over the cycle? Justify your answer.
solution:
6. Since the temperature of the gas increased in processes 1-2 and 2-3, and the heat capacity is positive, the gas received heat in these processes. In process 3-1, the temperature of the gas decreased, and the gas gave off heat. This means that the contact with the engine's heater was during the process $1-2-3$, and with the cooler - in process 3-1.

In all processes, the heat capacity of the gas changed, so to find the amount of heat received from the heater and given to the cooler, we will divide the temperature change interval into infinitesimally small intervals $\Delta T_{n}$, within which the heat capacity can be considered constant, and for each we will calculate the amount of heat received or given $\delta Q_{n}$ as

$$
\delta Q_{n}=C_{n} \delta T_{n}
$$

( $C_{n}$ - heat capacity of the gas on the $n$-th infinitesimally small interval) and sum these quantities

$$
Q=\sum_{n} \delta Q_{n}=\sum_{n} C_{n} \Delta T_{n}
$$

The sum (2) represents the area under the graph of the dependence of heat capacity on temperature - similar sums are calculated when determining the work of an elastic force as the area under the graph of the dependence of force on displacement. Therefore, the amount of heat received by the gas from the heater over the cycle $Q_{n}$ is the area under the graph of processes 1-2 and 2-3 (up to the temperature axis), and the amount of heat given by the gas to the cooler is the area under the graph of process 3-1 (up to the temperature axis). Since the figures under the graph are trapezoids, their areas can be found easily. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}
& Q_{h}=\frac{2 C_{0}+3 C_{0}}{2} \cdot T+\frac{3 C_{0}+C_{0}}{2} \cdot 3 T=\frac{17}{2} C_{0} T \\
& Q_{x}=\frac{2 C_{0}+C_{0}}{2} \cdot 4 T=\frac{12}{2} C_{0} T
\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we find the work done by the gas over the cycle

$$
A=Q_{H}-Q_{x}=\frac{5}{2} C_{0} T
$$

and the efficiency of the cycle $\eta$

$$
\eta=\frac{A}{Q_{H}}=\frac{5}{17}=0.29
$$

problem:
5. A sphere of radius $R$, made of a material with a density equal to that of water, floats in water, touching its surface (see figure). Find the force with which the water acts on the lower half of the sphere. The density of water $\rho$ is known.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_151e295255b2d1aa1930g-1.jpg?height=231&width=300&top_left_y=1666&top_left_x=153)
solution:
5. Obviously, the forces acting on different parts of the surface of the lower hemisphere from the water are different and are also directed differently. Therefore, calculating this force by summing the forces acting on small elements of the hemisphere's surface is quite complex. However, we have another method of summation. The fact is that similar sums of forces over the surface of a body are included in Archimedes' law. Therefore, if we take an auxiliary body such that the lower surface of the sphere is its surface, and use Archimedes' law, we can calculate the required force.

Thus, let's mentally cut and remove the upper hemisphere, i.e., consider a body in the form of only the lower hemisphere. On one hand, the Archimedes' force acting on this hemisphere from the water is known to us. This is

$$
F_{A}=\rho g V_{\text {n.u. }}=\frac{2}{3} \pi \rho g R^{3}
$$

where $\rho$ is the density of water, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity, and $V_{\text {n.u. }}=2 \pi R^{3} / 3$ is the volume of the hemisphere. On the other hand, this force is the resultant of the forces acting on the hemisphere from the liquid. Therefore, it can be represented as the sum of the forces, one of which acts on the lower surface of the hemisphere

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_0aa2685a2c7968513d04g-4.jpg?height=257&width=322&top_left_y=1216&top_left_x=1615)
$\vec{F}_{n . \text {.u. }}$. (which we need to find), and the second acts on its flat circular surface closing the hemisphere $\vec{F}_{k p}$. Since these forces are directed oppositely, in the expression for the Archimedes' force, they are subtracted

$$
F_{A}=F_{n . u .}-F_{k p}
$$

The last force is easy to calculate. Since the circular surface closing the hemisphere is at a depth of $R$, the hydrostatic pressure of the liquid at this depth is $p=\rho g R$. Therefore,

$$
F_{k p}=p \pi R^{2}=\pi \rho g R^{3}
$$

From here and formulas $(*),(* *)$ we find

$$
F_{n . u .}=F_{A}+F_{k p}=\frac{5}{3} \pi \rho g R^{3}
$$

problem:
5. A resistor with an unknown resistance was connected to a voltage source $U$, and two amperemeters $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{2}$ were connected in parallel (see the left diagram). In this case, the amperemeters show currents of $I_{1}=2$ A and $I_{2}=3$ A. Then, these amperemeters together with the same resistor
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_bea1dbb251077dbc2bb6g-1.jpg?height=230&width=700&top_left_y=1288&top_left_x=1240)
were connected in series and connected to the source (right diagram). In this case, amperemeter $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ shows a current of $I_{1}^{\prime}=4$ A. What current will flow in the circuit from the same source and resistor?
solution:
5. Obviously, ammeters have different resistances, since different currents flow through them when connected in parallel in the circuit. From Ohm's law for ammeters, it follows that the ratio of their resistances is

$$
\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{I_{2}}{I_{1}}=\frac{3}{2}
$$

Since the current flowing through the source in the first case is $I_{1}+I_{2}$, Ohm's law for the circuit segment in the first case gives

$$
r+\frac{R_{1} R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}=\frac{U}{I_{1}+I_{2}}
$$

or using (1)

$$
r+\frac{3}{5} R_{2}=\frac{U}{I_{1}+I_{2}}
$$

In the second case, the current through both ammeters and the source will be the same (series connection of elements). Therefore

$$
I_{2}^{\prime}=I_{1}^{\prime}=4 \mathrm{~A}
$$

Ohm's law for the second case gives

$$
r+R_{1}+R_{2}=\frac{U}{I_{1}^{\prime}}
$$

or using (1)

$$
r+\frac{5}{2} R_{2}=\frac{U}{I_{1}^{\prime}}
$$

Excluding the resistance of the second ammeter from the system of equations (2)-(3), we get

$$
r=\frac{U\left[25 I_{1}^{\prime}-6\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)\right]}{19 I_{1}^{\prime}\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)}
$$

From this, we find the current in the circuit if the source is short-circuited on the resistor

$$
I=\frac{U}{r}=\frac{19 I_{1}^{\prime}\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)}{25 I_{1}^{\prime}-6\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)}=12.7 \mathrm{~A}
$$

problem:
6. At the ends of a weightless, inextensible rod, a small body and a massive ring of the same mass are attached. The ring can move without friction along a horizontal rigid spoke in a gravitational field (see figure). At some moment, the ring and the body were given velocities $v$ and $2 v$, directed horizontally along the rod and opposite to each other (see figure). It is known that when the body rises to its maximum height, the rod makes an angle $\alpha$ with the spoke. Find the length of the rod.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_bea1dbb251077dbc2bb6g-1.jpg?height=343&width=385&top_left_y=1704&top_left_x=1535)
The spoke is very long.
solution:
6. At the moment of rising to the maximum height, the body moves horizontally. Therefore, from the condition of the inextensibility of the rod, we conclude that the speed is the same (their projections on the direction of the rod should be the same, and the speeds of the body and the ring at the moment of the body's rise to the maximum height are directed the same). From the law of conservation of momentum in the horizontal direction, we have

$$
2 m v - m v = 2 m v_{1}
$$

where \( v_{1} \) is the speed of the body and the ring at the moment of the body's rise to the maximum height. From this, we get

$$
v_{1} = \frac{v}{2}
$$

Now, using the law of conservation of energy, we obtain

$$
\frac{m v^{2}}{2} + \frac{m (2 v)^{2}}{2} = 2 \frac{m v_{1}^{2}}{2} + m g l (1 - \sin \alpha)
$$

where \( l \) is the length of the rod. From this, we find

$$
l = \frac{9 v^{2}}{4 g (1 - \sin \alpha)}
$$

problem: 1. Find all integer values of $x$ that are solutions to the equation $\sin (\pi(2 x-1))=\cos (\pi x / 2)$.
solution:
1. Answer: $x=4 t \pm 1, t \in Z$. Solution.

$\sin (\pi(2 x-1))=\sin (\pi(1-x) / 2) \rightarrow\left\{\begin{array}{l}2 x-1=(1-x) / 2+2 m \rightarrow 5 x / 2-2 m=3 / 2 \\ 2 x-1=(x+1) / 2+2 n \rightarrow 3 x / 2-2 n=3 / 2\end{array}\right.$

The equation $5 x-4 m=3$ in integers has the following solutions $\left\{\begin{array}{c}x=4 t+3 \\ m=5 t+3, t \in Z\end{array}\right.$.

The second equation $3 x-4 n=3$ in integers has solutions $\left\{\begin{array}{c}x=4 t+1 \\ m=3 t, t \in Z\end{array}\right.$.

Combining the solutions, we get the answer $x=4 t \pm 1, t \in Z$.

problem: 3. A sealed horizontal cylindrical vessel of length $l$ is divided into two parts by a movable partition. On one side of the partition, there is 1 mole of oxygen, and on the other side, there is 1 mole of helium and 1 mole of oxygen, with the partition being in equilibrium. At some point in time, the partition becomes permeable to helium and remains impermeable to oxygen. Find the displacement of the partition. The temperatures of the gases are the same and do not change during the process.
solution:
3. From the condition of equilibrium of the partition (equality of pressures to the right and left of it), we find that initially it is located at a distance of $2 l / 3$ and $l/3$ from the ends of the vessel. After helium is uniformly distributed throughout the vessel, its partial pressures to the right and left of the partition (regardless of its position) will be equal. Therefore, the partition will be positioned such that the partial pressures of oxygen to the right and left are the same. Since the amounts of oxygen substance to the right and left of the partition are the same, it will be positioned in the middle. Consequently, the displacement of the partition after the redistribution of helium is

$$
\Delta x=\frac{2 l}{3}-\frac{l}{2}=\frac{l}{6}
$$

problem:
4. A small weightless ring is hinged to a light rod of length $2 l$. At the midpoint and end of the rod, point masses of $m$ and $2 m$ are fixed. The ring is placed on a smooth horizontal rod. Initially, the rod was held horizontally and then released. Find the speed of the ring at the moment when the rod passes the vertical position. Assume the mass of the rod is zero.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_0209b43e87d803cc3743g-1.jpg?height=109&width=349&top_left_y=1182&top_left_x=1593)
solution:
4. Since the external forces on the system of bodies and the spoke act only in the vertical direction (the gravitational forces of the bodies and the reaction force of the rod), the projection of the momentum of the system of bodies on the horizontal direction is conserved. Therefore, if the lower body has a speed $v$ (which is obviously directed to the left) at the moment the spoke passes through the vertical position, the middle body has a speed $2 v$, directed to the right. The speeds of the bodies can be found using the law of conservation of mechanical energy

$$
\frac{2 m v^{2}}{2}+\frac{m(2 v)^{2}}{2}=5 m g l
$$

From this, we find

$$
v=\sqrt{\frac{5 g l}{3}}
$$

The speed of the ring is easiest to find by transitioning to a reference frame associated with the central body. In this reference frame, the middle body is at rest, while the lower body and the ring move in opposite directions with the same speeds. On the other hand, the speed of the lower body in this reference frame is directed to the left and equals $3 v$. Therefore, the speed of the ring is also $3 v$, but directed to the right. Therefore, in the reference frame associated with the Earth, the speed of the ring is

$$
v_{\kappa}=5 v=5 \sqrt{\frac{5 g l}{3}}=\sqrt{\frac{125 g l}{3}}
$$

problem: Task 1. The administration divided the region into several districts based on the principle: the population of a large district exceeds $8 \%$ of the region's population and for any large district, there are two non-large districts with a combined population that is larger. Into what minimum number of districts was the region divided?
solution:
Answer: 8 districts.

Solution. The number of "small" districts is no less than 2 according to the condition, and their population does not exceed $8 \%$ of the total population of the region. We will show that the number of districts in the region is no less than 8. If the number of districts in the region is no more than 7, but there are no more than 5 "large" districts with a population of less than $16 \%$ each. Then the total population of the region cannot amount to $100 \%$. Indeed, $2 \cdot 8 \%+5 \cdot 16 \%=96 \%<100 \%$. Thus, the number of districts in the region is no less than 8. A division into 8 districts is possible, for example, $8 \%+8 \%+14 \%+14 \%+14 \%+14 \%+14 \%+14 \%=100 \%$.

problem: Problem 2. The number $x$ satisfies the condition $\frac{\sin 3 x}{\sin x}=\frac{5}{3}$. Find the value of the expression $\frac{\cos 5 x}{\cos x}$ for such $x$
solution:
Answer: $-\frac{11}{9}$.

Solution.

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \sin x \neq 0 \rightarrow \frac{\sin 3 x}{\sin x}=\frac{3 \sin x-4 \sin ^{3} x}{\sin x}=3-4 \sin ^{2} x \rightarrow 3-4 \sin ^{2} x=\frac{5}{3} \rightarrow \sin ^{2} x=\frac{1}{3} \rightarrow \\
& \rightarrow \cos ^{2} x=\frac{2}{3} \rightarrow \cos 2 x=\frac{1}{3} ; \\
& \frac{\cos 5 x}{\cos x}=\frac{\cos (3 x+2 x)}{\cos x}=\frac{\cos (3 x+2 x)}{\cos x}=\frac{\cos 3 x \cos 2 x-\sin 3 x \sin 2 x}{\cos x}= \\
& \frac{\left(4 \cos ^{3} x-3 \cos x\right) \cos 2 x-2 \sin 3 x \sin x \cos x}{\cos x}=\left(4 \cos ^{2} x-3\right) \cos 2 x-2 \sin 3 x \sin x= \\
& =(2 \cos 2 x-1) \cos 2 x-\cos 2 x+\cos 4 x==(2 \cos 2 x-1) \cos 2 x-\cos 2 x+2 \cos ^{2} 2 x-1= \\
& =\left(\frac{2}{3}-1\right) \cdot \frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{9}-1=-\frac{11}{9} .
\end{aligned}
$$

problem: Problem 1. Seven students in the class receive one two every two days of study, and nine other students receive one two every three days each. The rest of the students in the class never receive twos. From Monday to Friday, 30 new twos appeared in the journal. How many new twos will appear in the class journal on Saturday?
solution:
Answer: 9

Solution. Over the period from Monday to Saturday (six days), in the journal, there will be 3 new twos from each student of the first group (seven people) and 2 new twos from each of the 9 students of the second group. The total number of new twos for the school week is $7 \cdot 3 + 9 \cdot 2 = 39$. Then, on Saturday, the journal will have $39 - 30 = 9$ new twos.

Problem 2. Prove that for any positive numbers $a$ and $b$ the following inequality holds

$$
\sqrt{\frac{a^{2}}{b}}+\sqrt{\frac{b^{2}}{a}} \geq \sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}
$$
solution:
Solution. Let $b \geq a$. Divide the inequality by $\sqrt{a}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}+\sqrt{\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}} \geq 1+\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}} \rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}-1\right) \geq 1-\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}} \rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{b}{a}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}}(\sqrt{b}-\sqrt{a}) \geq \frac{(\sqrt{b}-\sqrt{a})}{\sqrt{b}} \rightarrow \\
& \rightarrow \frac{b}{a}(\sqrt{b}-\sqrt{a}) \geq(\sqrt{b}-\sqrt{a}) \rightarrow(\sqrt{b}-\sqrt{a})\left(\frac{b}{a}-1\right) \geq 0
\end{aligned}
$$

The last inequality is true. The case $a \geq b$ is analogous.

problem: Problem 3. Through the vertex $B$ of an equilateral triangle $ABC$, a line $L$ is drawn, intersecting the extension of side $AC$ beyond point $C$. The lines $MC$ and $NA$ intersect at a common point $D$ and intersect the sides $AB$ and $BC$ of the triangle at points $P$ and $Q$ respectively. solution:
# Answer: 1.

Solution. Triangles $M B C$ and $A B N$ are isosceles, therefore

$$
\begin{gathered}
\angle B M C = \angle B C M = \alpha \rightarrow \angle N B C = 2 \alpha, \angle B A N = \angle B N A = \beta \rightarrow \angle A B M = 2 \beta \\
2 \alpha + 2 \beta + 60^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 60^{\circ}
\end{gathered}
$$

In triangle $M D N$, angle $P D Q$ is $180^{\circ} - \alpha - \beta = 120^{\circ}$, and the sum of the opposite angles of quadrilateral $P B Q D$ is $180^{\circ}$, so a circle can be circumscribed around it.

By the Law of Sines, $P Q = 2 R \sin 120^{\circ} = \sqrt{3} \rightarrow R = 1$.

problem: 3. (physics) Two weightless glasses with different amounts of water are balanced on a lever of unequal-arm scales with a length of $L$. A mass of water $m$ is transferred from one glass to the other, and the scales lose their balance. To restore balance, the fulcrum of the lever needs to be moved by a distance $l$ relative to its old position. Find the total mass of water in the glasses. Neglect the mass of the lever of the scales.
solution:
Solution. Let the mass of water in the left glass be $m_{1}$, in the right glass be $m_{2}$, and the lever arms of the glasses be $l_{1}$ and $L-l_{1}$, respectively. Then the condition

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_f912147981c7262840e0g-2.jpg?height=137&width=557&top_left_y=865&top_left_x=1338)
for equilibrium of the balance in the first case gives

$$
m_{1} l_{1}=m_{2}\left(L-l_{1}\right)
$$

Suppose we pour a mass of water $m$ from the left glass to the right glass. Then the condition for equilibrium of the balance in the second case gives

$$
\left(m_{1}-m\right)\left(l_{1}+l\right)=\left(m_{2}+m\right)\left(L-l_{1}-l\right)
$$

Subtracting the first equation from the second, we find the total mass of water in the glasses

$$
m_{1}+m_{2}=\frac{m L}{l}
$$

problem: 4. (physics) From a piece of metal with mass $M$, a rectangular parallelepiped is cast. Then, a source of constant voltage is connected to different pairs of mutually opposite faces of the parallelepiped. It turned out that the ratio of the thermal powers dissipated in the parallelepiped when the source is connected to different pairs of faces is 1:2:8. Find the lengths of the edges of the parallelepiped. The density of the metal $\rho$ is known. The parallelepiped is connected to the source using wide bus bars that ensure the source contacts the entire area of the face, allowing the effects of current spreading to be neglected.
solution:
Solution. Let the edge lengths of the parallelepiped be $a$ (the smallest), $b$ (the middle), and $c$ (the largest). Then the resistance of the parallelepiped when electrical contacts are connected to the faces with sides $a$ and $b$ is

$$
R_{a b}=\frac{\rho_{0} a b}{c}
$$

where $\rho_{0}$ is the resistivity of the metal. Similarly, we find the resistance of the parallelepiped when electrical contacts are connected to other pairs of faces

$$
R_{a c}=\frac{\rho_{0} a c}{b}, \quad R_{b c}=\frac{\rho_{0} b c}{a}
$$

Obviously, the resistance values satisfy the following inequalities

$$
R_{a b}P_{a c}>P_{b c}
$$

where $P_{a b}, P_{a c}$, and $P_{b c}$ are the powers dissipated in the parallelepiped when electrical contacts are connected to the faces with sides $a$ and $b\left(P_{a b}\right)$, $a$ and $c\left(P_{a c}\right)$, and $b$ and $c\left(P_{b c}\right)$. Therefore, from the problem statement, we get

$$
\frac{P_{a c}}{P_{b c}}=\frac{R_{b c}}{R_{a c}}=\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}=2 \text { and } \frac{P_{a b}}{P_{a c}}=\frac{R_{a c}}{R_{a b}}=\frac{c^{2}}{b^{2}}=4
$$

or $b=\sqrt{2} a, c=2 b=2 \sqrt{2} a$. Since

$$
a b c=\frac{M}{\rho}
$$

we find

$$
a=\left(\frac{M}{4 \rho}\right)^{1 / 3}, b=\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{M}{4 \rho}\right)^{1 / 3}, c=2 \sqrt{2}\left(\frac{M}{4 \rho}\right)^{1 / 3}
$$

5. Two loads with masses $m$ and $2 m$ are connected by three threads as shown in the figure. The thread $\mathrm{AB}$ is horizontal, and the thread CD forms an angle $\alpha$ with the vertical. Find the tensions in the threads AB and CD. The thread AB is cut. Find the accelerations of the loads immediately after this. The threads are inextensible and weightless.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_5a5c4a883292a9d82de7g-1.jpg?height=401&width=386&top_left_y=1224&top_left_x=1516)
solution:
5. First, let's find the forces acting in all threads in equilibrium. On the body of mass \( m \), the force of gravity \( m \vec{g} \) and three tension forces of the threads \( \vec{T}_{A B}, \vec{T}_{C D} \), and the tension force of the lower thread, equal to \( 2 m \vec{g} \) (see the figure). Therefore, the equilibrium condition for this body in projections on the horizontal and vertical directions gives

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_1c50a76ea7b7bad6fbcag-3.jpg?height=406&width=383&top_left_y=2344&top_left_x=1542)

\[
\begin{aligned}
& T_{A B}=T_{C D} \sin \alpha \\
& 3 m g=T_{C D} \cos \alpha
\end{aligned}
\]

From these formulas, we find

\[
T_{C D}=\frac{3 m g}{\cos \alpha}, \quad T_{A B}=3 m g \operatorname{tg} \alpha
\]

Immediately after cutting the thread \( \mathrm{AB} \), the body of mass \( m \) will start moving under the action of two forces: \( 3 m \vec{g} \), directed vertically downward, and \( \vec{T}_{C D} \), directed along the thread CD. Since the velocity of the body is zero, the vector of its acceleration is perpendicular to the thread CD. And since the tension force in the lower thread does not change immediately after cutting the thread \( \mathrm{AB} \) (for the tension forces to change, the bodies must move), the second law of Newton for the body of mass \( m \) in projections on the direction perpendicular to the thread \( \mathrm{CD} \) gives

\[
m a_{m}=3 m g \sin \alpha
\]

From this, we get

\[
a_{m}=3 g \sin \alpha
\]

Due to the fact that the tension force in the thread connecting the bodies does not change, the acceleration of the body of mass \( 2 m \) is zero

\[
a_{2 m}=0
\]

$$

$$
t_{\text {poli }}=t_{2}+t_{1}
$$

From formula (1) and the law of velocity change for uniformly accelerated motion, we find the change in the vertical component of the body's velocity over the time of ascent to the maximum height:

$$
0=v_{0, y}-\frac{g\left(t_{2}+t_{1}\right)}{2}
$$

where $v_{0, y}$ is the projection of the initial velocity vector onto the vertical axis. From this, we find the vertical component of the initial velocity of the body

$$
v_{0, y}=\frac{g\left(t_{2}+t_{1}\right)}{2}
$$

The horizontal component of the initial velocity can be found as follows. Since from the moment $t_{1}$ to the moment of ascent to the maximum height (i.e., over the time $\left.\left(t_{2}-t_{1}\right) / 2\right)$ the vertical component decreases to zero, applying the law of motion for velocity to this stage of motion, we get

$$
0=v_{1, y}-\frac{g\left(t_{2}-t_{1}\right)}{2}
$$

where $v_{1, y}$ is the vertical component of the velocity vector of the body at the moment $t_{1}$. Therefore,

$$
v_{1, y}=\frac{g\left(t_{2}-t_{1}\right)}{2}
$$

Therefore, the horizontal component of the velocity of the body at this moment is

$$
v_{1, x}=v_{1, y} \operatorname{ctg} \alpha=\frac{g\left(t_{2}-t_{1}\right)}{2} \sqrt{3}=v_{0, x}
$$

Since the horizontal component of the velocity does not change, it will be (3) throughout the motion. From here and formulas (2) we find the range of flight $S$

$$
S=v_{0, x_{\text {poli }}}=\frac{g\left(t_{2}-t_{1}\right)}{2} \sqrt{3}\left(t_{2}+t_{1}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} g\left(t_{2}^{2}-t_{1}^{2}\right)
$$

The maximum height of ascent $h$ can be found knowing the vertical component of the initial velocity

$$
h=\frac{v_{0, y}^{2}}{2 g}=\frac{g\left(t_{2}+t_{1}\right)^{2}}{8}
$$

problem:
5. A resistor with an unknown resistance was connected to an electrical voltage source $U$, and two amperemeters $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{2}$ were connected in parallel (see the left figure). In this case, the amperemeters show currents of $I_{1}=2$ A and $I_{2}=3$ A. Then, these amperemeters, together with the same
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_ac1250e2e5d2cdfd695dg-1.jpg?height=232&width=698&top_left_y=1474&top_left_x=1240)
resistor, are connected in series and connected to the source (right figure). In this case, amperemeter $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ shows a current of $I_{1}^{\prime}=4$ A. What current will flow in the circuit from the same source and resistor, but without the amperemeters?
solution:
5. Obviously, ammeters have different resistances, since different currents flow through them when connected in parallel in the circuit. From Ohm's law for ammeters, it follows that the ratio of their resistances is

$$
\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{I_{2}}{I_{1}}=\frac{3}{2}
$$

Since the current flowing through the source in the first case is $I_{1}+I_{2}$, Ohm's law for the circuit segment in the first case gives

$$
r+\frac{R_{1} R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}=\frac{U}{I_{1}+I_{2}}
$$

or using (1)

$$
r+\frac{3}{5} R_{2}=\frac{U}{I_{1}+I_{2}}
$$

In the second case, the current through both ammeters and the source will be the same (series connection of elements). Therefore

$$
I_{2}^{\prime}=I_{1}^{\prime}=4 \mathrm{~A}
$$

Ohm's law for the second case gives

$$
r+R_{1}+R_{2}=\frac{U}{I_{1}^{\prime}}
$$

or using (1)

$$
r+\frac{5}{2} R_{2}=\frac{U}{I_{1}^{\prime}}
$$

Excluding the resistance of the second ammeter from the system of equations (2)-(3), we get

$$
r=\frac{U\left[25 I_{1}^{\prime}-6\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)\right]}{19 I_{1}^{\prime}\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)}
$$

From this, we find the current in the circuit if the source is short-circuited on the resistor

$$
I=\frac{U}{r}=\frac{19 I_{1}^{\prime}\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)}{25 I_{1}^{\prime}-6\left(I_{1}+I_{2}\right)}=12.7 \mathrm{~A}
$$

problem:
6. At the ends of a weightless, inextensible rod, a small body and a massive ring of the same mass are attached. The ring can move without friction along a horizontal rigid spoke in a gravitational field (see figure). At some moment, the ring and the body were given velocities $v$ and $2 v$, directed horizontally along the rod and opposite to each other (see figure). It is known that when the body rises to its maximum height, the rod makes an angle $\alpha$ with the spoke. Find

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_ac1250e2e5d2cdfd695dg-1.jpg?height=346&width=382&top_left_y=1916&top_left_x=1497)
the length of the rod. The spoke is very long.
solution:
6. At the moment of reaching the maximum height, the body moves horizontally. Therefore, from the condition of the inextensibility of the rod, we conclude that the speed is the same (their projections on the direction of the rod should be the same, and the speeds of the body and the ring at the moment the body reaches the maximum height are directed the same). From the law of conservation of momentum in the horizontal direction, we have

$$
2 m v - m v = 2 m v_{1}
$$

where \( v_{1} \) is the speed of the body and the ring at the moment the body reaches the maximum height. From this, we get

$$
v_{1} = \frac{v}{2}
$$

Now, using the law of conservation of energy, we obtain

$$
\frac{m v^{2}}{2} + \frac{m (2 v)^{2}}{2} = 2 \frac{m v_{1}^{2}}{2} + m g l (1 - \sin \alpha)
$$

where \( l \) is the length of the rod. From this, we find

$$
l = \frac{9 v^{2}}{4 g (1 - \sin \alpha)}
$$

problem: 2. In a garden partnership, they decided to make a pond using water from a spring. All the water from the spring was directed into the pond using a pipeline, and the pond began to fill with water. As a result, after \( t = 16 \) days, the pond was filled to \( 2 / 3 \) of its volume. At this moment, it was noticed that one quarter of the water from the spring was leaking through the pipeline. The leaks were fixed. How long after this did the pond fill up?
solution:
2. Let the volume of the pond be $V$, and the volume of water flowing out of the source per unit time be $w$. Since before the leak was sealed, three-quarters of the water from the spring entered the pond, we have

$$
\frac{3}{4} w t = \frac{2}{3} V \quad \Rightarrow \quad \frac{9}{8} t = \frac{V}{w}
$$

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_0e208de39d119289f7e1g-1.jpg?height=591&width=836&top_left_y=367&top_left_x=1087)

After the leak was sealed, all the water started entering the pond. Therefore, for the time $t_{1}$ required to completely fill the pond, we have

$$
w t_{1} = \frac{1}{3} V \quad \Rightarrow \quad 3 t_{1} = \frac{V}{w}
$$

By equating the left sides of these equations, we get

$$
t_{1} = \frac{3}{8} t
$$

problem: 3. Two people simultaneously step onto an escalator from opposite ends, which is moving downward at a speed of $u=1.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The person moving downward has a speed of $v=3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ relative to the escalator, while the person moving upward has a speed of $2 v / 3$ relative to the escalator. At what distance from the bottom of the escalator will they meet? The length of the escalator is $l=100 \mathrm{~m}$.
solution:
3. The speeds of the people relative to the ground are

$$
\text { descending } v_{c n}=v+u \text {, ascending } v_{\text {nоо }}=\frac{2}{3} v-u \text {. }
$$

Therefore, the time it takes for the people to meet is

$$
t=\frac{l}{v_{c n}+v_{n o d}}=\frac{3 l}{5 v}
$$

And since the ascending person will travel a distance until the meeting

$$
l_{\text {noo }}=v_{\text {noo }} t=\frac{3 l}{5 v}\left(\frac{2}{3} v-u\right)=10 \mathrm{M} .
$$

problem:
4. A body of mass $m$ is attached to one end of a weightless, inextensible string, the other end of which is attached to the ceiling. The string is passed over a pulley of mass $M$, which is concentrated on its axis. At the initial moment, the body is held and then released. Find the accelerations of the body and the pulley.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_98019744d8c01484e6a0g-1.jpg?height=171&width=1077&top_left_y=1202&top_left_x=158)
solution:
4. It is clear that the bodies will not fall freely with the acceleration due to gravity, and the string will be taut. Indeed, if the pulley falls with an acceleration of $g$, then on the side where the body is located, such a length of the string is "stretched" that the acceleration of the body should equal $2g$, which means that the string is taut, forcing the body to have an acceleration greater than $g$, and the pulley to have an acceleration less than $g$.

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2024_05_06_0e208de39d119289f7e1g-1.jpg?height=340&width=257&top_left_y=2189&top_left_x=1685)

The body is acted upon by the force of gravity $m \vec{g}$ and the tension force of the string $\vec{T}$. The pulley is acted upon by the force of gravity $M \vec{g}$ and two tension forces of the string $\vec{T}^{\prime}$, which are equal to each other since the mass of the pulley is concentrated on the axis, and equal in magnitude to the tension force acting on the body. Therefore, Newton's second law for the body and the pulley, projected onto the vertical axis, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
& m a_{1}=m g+T \\
& M a_{2}=M g-2 T
\end{aligned}
$$

Considering that the acceleration of the body is twice the acceleration of the pulley, we get

$$
a_{1}=\frac{2(2 m+M) g}{4 m+M}, \quad a_{2}=\frac{(2 m+M) g}{4 m+M}
$$

problem: 1. Find the number of points in the $x O y$ plane having natural coordinates $(x, y)$ and lying on the parabola $y=-\frac{x^{2}}{4}+11 x+23$.
solution:
Answer: 22.

Solution. Let's find those values of $x$ for which $y$ is positive: $-\frac{x^{2}}{4}+11 x+23>0 \Leftrightarrow-\frac{1}{4}(x+2)(x-46)>0$, from which $-2<x<46$. On this interval, there are 45 natural values of $x: x=1, x=2, \ldots, x=45$. In this interval, $y$ takes integer values only for even $x$ - a total of 22 possibilities. solution:

Solution. The given equation is equivalent to the following

$$

solution:
Solution. Let $\sqrt{\frac{y}{x}}=u, \sqrt{x y}=v \quad$ (with $u>0, \quad v>0$). Then $\quad u v=\sqrt{\frac{y}{x}} \cdot \sqrt{x y}=\sqrt{y^{2}}=|y|=y$, $\frac{v}{u}=\sqrt{x y}: \sqrt{\frac{y}{x}}=\sqrt{x^{2}}=|x|=x$, since by the condition $x$ and $y$ are positive. The system takes the form

$$

\end{array} \Leftrightarrow \left\{\begin{array}{l}

3 v^{4} + u^{4} v^{4} = 84
\end{array}\right.\right.
